name: RFdiffusion
org: University of Washington (Institute for Protein Design)
one_liner: An SE(3) diffusion network generates 3D protein backbones, ProteinMPNN designs matching amino-acid sequences, and AlphaFold2 self-consistency filters select candidates for wet-lab validation.

loop.proposes: 3D protein backbone coordinates (residue translations and orientations) generated by an SE(3) diffusion model fine-tuned from RoseTTAFold, paired with ProteinMPNN sequences
loop.judged_by: AlphaFold2 / RoseTTAFold structure-prediction self-consistency (backbone RMSD and interface confidence pAE) followed by wet-lab expression, biolayer interferometry and cryo-EM
loop.steers: Computational self-consistency metrics prune thousands of sampled trajectories down to top designs for physical synthesis and binding assays

headline_result: In Nature (2023), RFdiffusion designed de novo protein binders across five therapeutic and viral targets with an experimental hit rate of roughly 19% when testing 95 designs per target (two to three orders of magnitude higher than classical Rosetta binder design), and a cryo-EM structure of a designed Influenza HA binder (PDB: 8SK7) matched the design model at atomic accuracy (1.45 A backbone RMSD).
caveat: Passing the AlphaFold2 computational filter does not ensure wet-lab binding (around four in five filtered binder designs still fail in vitro), and scaffolding full multi-step catalytic enzyme active sites in the lab requires additional physics and screening beyond backbone diffusion.
beyond_harness_note: The generator is an SE(3) geometric diffusion model over 3D protein coordinates rather than a language model, and structural fold prediction plus biophysical assays filter the population to produce physical protein sequences.
generative_model: SE(3)-equivariant diffusion model fine-tuned from RoseTTAFold structure-prediction weights, coupled with ProteinMPNN graph neural network sequence design (not an LLM)
algorithmic_authority: AlphaFold2 structural self-consistency and interface pAE filtering, plus wet-lab biolayer interferometry, circular dichroism and cryo-EM

sources.title: De novo design of protein structure and function with RFdiffusion (Nature, 2023)

verification.notes: Verified against Watson, Juergens, Bennett, Trippe, Yim et al., Nature 620, 1089-1100 (2023), doi:10.1038/s41586-023-06415-8, and RosettaCommons/RFdiffusion. Confirmed 95 designs tested per binder target, ~19% experimental binder hit rate across 5 targets, and Influenza HA cryo-EM structure PDB 8SK7 matching design within 1.45 A.
